keys.description: When true, this MCP server lists the top-level lead session it serves on the machine's dashboard (one daemon per OS environment, serving local web pages for the workflow sessions on it) and opens the browser for it; when false, it does neither. The daemon itself runs either way: the plugin launcher starts it when none runs and keeps it current, since the daemon also hosts every session's MCP server, so this key never starts, stops, or replaces it. Whether a session is listed is read for that session, a session-scope tune included: the session's own tune applies at once, any other change at the session's next tool call a minute or more later, and turning it off also applies within a few minutes without one. A session whose value is false is never listed, and this server sends the daemon nothing about it. MCP tools behave the same either way. When this key's manifest fails to load, the dashboard stays off.

TCP port the dashboard daemon listens on, on the loopback interface; 0 always uses a port the OS assigns. When the port is taken, the daemon falls back to the port the last daemon used, then to an OS-assigned port, so a restart keeps its address while the configured port stays taken; a free configured port always wins, and the daemon records the port it uses in its endpoint file. Read from the project, global, and built-in values when the plugin launcher starts the daemon (none running, or an older one), so a running daemon keeps its port until it is next started.

When true, the dashboard daemon listens on this machine's network interfaces as well, so another device on the network can open its pages with an access token, while a browser on this machine still opens them at localhost with no token. Only the global value applies: a project, repo, or session value is refused on write and ignored, since one daemon serves every session on the machine. The daemon re-reads the value whenever a session connects to it and, when the value differs from its own mode, replaces itself with one in the new mode, letting the calls in flight finish and reconnecting its sessions, so a change applies at the next session start. The access token is shown only on the dashboard's index page viewed on this machine and persists across daemon restarts in the daemon's state directory; deleting its file issues a new one.

Minutes a message may remain unread in its recipient's mailbox queue before the daemon sends its sender one system notice. The message stays queued and may still be read; a late read sends no follow-up notice. System mail never triggers notices. Only the global value applies, since the daemon serves every project on the machine. Read again every sweep (30 seconds), so a tune applies without a restart.

Most disk space, in MiB, one daemon-hosted session's audit record may use. The audit record keeps every tool call, tool result and hidden harness event of a session the dashboard daemon hosts, with recognized secrets masked before they are written (masking is best-effort: a secret in an unrecognized shape is kept as written). When a session's record would grow past this size, its oldest records are removed first, a segment at a time. The value that applies is the smaller of this and dashboard.audit_total_cap_mib, and at least 4. The per-body cap must stay at most 1/16 of it: a write that breaks this is refused, and a stored set that breaks it is adjusted to the nearest valid values with a warning in the daemon log. Only the global value applies, since one daemon serves every session on the machine; read when the daemon starts.

Most disk space, in MiB, all sessions' audit records together may use. When a new record would pass this size, the daemon removes whole sessions' audit records, the least recently active first, keeping the session being written for last; that session alone keeps at least its newest segment. Only audit records are removed; conversations and their history stay. The same consistency rule as dashboard.audit_session_cap_mib applies. Only the global value applies; read when the daemon starts.

Most stored size, in KiB, of each tool input, tool output or raw line in the audit record, measured as written to disk. A longer body is stored as its first and last halves with a marker giving its full size; the middle is not kept and cannot be searched. Secrets are masked over the whole body before it is cut. It must stay at most 1/16 of the effective per-session cap (see dashboard.audit_session_cap_mib). Only the global value applies; read when the daemon starts.

Days a session's audit record is kept after the session was last seen (registered, heartbeating, ended or captured). After that the whole record is removed, even when the session's conversation is kept longer, and deleting a session removes its record at once. A record a session deleted by an older daemon left behind ages out by this period. A shorter period limits how long masked-but-imperfect secret handling keeps data on disk. Only the global value applies; read when the daemon starts and checked hourly.
When true, the dashboard shows the companion character beside the conversation. Only the global value applies.

Deprecated alias of dashboard.companion_enabled, kept so 0.51.0 clients and scripts keep working: off hides the companion; visual and full both show it and behave the same. A write to either key updates the other, and a value stored here by an older version decides whether the companion shows. Use dashboard.companion_enabled instead. Only the global value applies.

Selects what drives the companion: rules (built-in reactions to session events) or agent (a separate lightweight agent writes the reactions). The 0.51.0 values sidecar and lead-tool are deprecated; config.tune still accepts them and stores rules. Only the global value applies.
Selects the companion pack: default, auto, or a pack ID. Auto selects a pack for the visible session. Only the global value applies.
Selects the companion preset by ID. Only the global value applies.
Selects the companion outfit set by ID. Empty follows the preset, and an ID the active pack does not define is ignored. Only the global value applies.
Selects the companion hair set by ID. Empty follows the preset, and an ID the active pack does not define is ignored. Only the global value applies.
Selects the companion eye set by ID. Empty follows the preset, and an ID the active pack does not define is ignored. Only the global value applies.
Chooses companion attachments as up to 16 space-separated <slot>=<id> pairs, one attachment per slot; the ID none clears that slot. Empty follows the preset. Only the global value applies.
Overrides companion tint channel colors as up to 16 space-separated <channel>=#rrggbb pairs. Empty follows the preset. Only the global value applies.
Minimum seconds between two calls of the agent companion director; a trigger inside the cooldown is dropped. Only the global value applies.
Maximum calls of the agent companion director in a rolling hour; a trigger over the cap is dropped. Only the global value applies.

Companion pack sources the companion settings list for install: a whitespace-separated list of at most 16 https URLs, each a git repository (with an optional #ref) or a zip file holding a marketplace.json. A source is fetched only when the user asks to list, install, or update its packs. An invalid entry is shown as an error and skipped. Only the global value applies.

Selects the active companion Portable Soul ID. Empty resolves to default, auto-created from the active pack's starter persona on first use without overwriting an existing Soul. Only the global value applies.
Overrides the root directory storing companion Portable Soul folders (for example a Git-synced path). Empty uses ~/.ws/companion-soul. Only the global value applies.

Agent tier for the Lightweight Cosmetic Puppeteer (body) that drives VRM reactions and stage speech quips: empty or auto picks the small tier on the first available harness, or name <harness>.<tier>, a bare tier, an agent.tier_aliases name, or an agent.tier_routing token. Applies at the next companion reaction; a value that cannot launch falls back to auto with a reason shown in Settings. Only the global value applies.

Agent tier for the High-Tier Mobile Full Lead (brain) powering Companion Messenger, Soul/Episodes memory, and background subagent orchestration: empty or auto picks the medium tier on the first available harness, or name <harness>.<tier>, a bare tier, an agent.tier_aliases name, or an agent.tier_routing token. Applies at the next companion handoff or launch; a value that cannot launch falls back to auto with a reason shown in Settings. Only the global value applies.

Legacy single speech-to-text backend for dashboard composer voice typing (for example openai_api, groq, openrouter, native, or local/<name>). Honored when dashboard.voice_backend_order is unset; otherwise dashboard.voice_backend_order takes precedence. Only the global value applies.

Ordered priority list of speech-to-text backends for dashboard composer voice typing, as whitespace-separated backend IDs (for example native openrouter openai_api groq local/<name>). The first backend available in the current environment is used. When empty, falls back to dashboard.voice_backend if set, or native by default. Only the global value applies.

When true, OpenRouter voice transcription may reuse the Werk OpenRouter API key (configured in Account) instead of requiring a dedicated OpenRouter (Voice) key. Default false so configuring the Werk key never silently enables paid voice transcription. Only the global value applies.

Overrides the transcription model sent to the selected voice backend (for example gpt-transcribe, whisper-large-v3-turbo, or an OpenRouter/local model ID). Empty uses the backend's default model. Only the global value applies.

Language hint for voice transcription (ISO-639-1/BCP-47 code, or comma-separated codes for OpenAI gpt-transcribe). Empty lets the backend auto-detect the spoken language. Only the global value applies.
